questions.question: Rudrasena II of which of the following dynasties married Prabhavatigupta, the daughter of Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vakataka**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II of the Vakataka dynasty: 
 
• Prabhavati Gupta
 
 
• The daughter of Chandragupta II, the ruler of the Gupta Empire, and queen Kuberanaga.
 
• She was a powerful monarch in early Indian history. 
 
 
 
• Rudrasena II
 
 
• The ruler of the Pravarapura-Nandivardhana branch of the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• He ruled in the Deccan region to the south of the Gupta empire. 
 
• Rudrasena II's reign was short, from around 385–390 CE.
 
• He died early, leaving his sons Divakarasena, Damodarasena, and Pravarasena II minors.
 
 
 
• Prabhavati Gupta ruled as regent for an extended period of time. 
 
• Rudrasena became a devotee of Chakrapani or Vishnu, unlike his ancestors who were all devout Shaivites.
 
• His change of faith was probably encouraged by his father-in-law and his queen, who were both staunch Vaishnavites. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pushyabhuti
 
 
• Also known as the Vardhana dynasty, this dynasty ruled in northern India during the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• The dynasty's last ruler, Harsha Vardhana, ruled from Kanyakubja (modern-day Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh) and extended his empire to Kamarupa in the east and Narmada River in the south. 
 
 
 
• Chalukya
 
 
• This dynasty ruled in central and southern India, consolidating its power after defeating the Pallavas and the Gangas.
 
• The Chalukyas expanded their power over the Deccan Plateau after Pulakesin I. 
 
 
 
• Pallava
 
 
• This dynasty ruled in northern Tamil Nadu and was a major power for a brief time.
 
• The Pallavas' art and architecture include the Vaikuntha Perumal Temple at Kanchipuram, the Shore Temple, and the Pancha Rathas of Mahabalipuram

questions.question: Madhuri Barthwal, a folk singer and Padma Shri 2022 awardee, belongs to which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Madhuri Barthwal is a **folk singer from Uttarakhand, India.**
 
• **She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 **for her contributions to the preservation and promotion of folk music in the region. 
 
• **She was the first woman to become a music composer for All India Radio. **
 
• She is **also said to be the first female musician** from Uttarakhand to become a music teacher. 
 
• **She was awarded the Nari Shakti Puraskar in 2019 by Ram Nath Kovind. **
 
• She has** also received the Uttarakhand Ratna** and **Uttarakhand Bhushan awards. **
 
• She **has documented and taught folk music traditions**, and has also written five books on Garhwali folk music. 
 
• Her research work, Raag Raganiya in Garhwali folk songs, explains how Indian classical ragas have been incorporated into Garhwali folk song

questions.question: Which of the following options is the legislative organ of the Union government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legislative organ of the Union government is Parliament.
 
• Parliament is made up of the President, the Rajya Sabha, and the Lok Sabha: 
 
• Rajya Sabha
 
 
• Also known as the Council of States, this is the upper house of Parliament.
 
• It has 245 members, with 233 representing states and union territories and 12 nominated by the President.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is permanent and cannot be dissolved. 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha
 
 
• Also known as the House of the People, this is the lower house of Parliament.
 
• It is a temporary house that can be dissolved if the party in power loses the support of the majority of the house. 
 
 
 
• President
 
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha. 
 
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India and the highest representative authority of the people.
 
• However, the Supreme Court can review Parliament's laws, and the President and Vice President are part of the Executive branch. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Judiciary
 
 
• Interprets laws, settles disputes, and administers justice.
 
• For example, the Supreme Court interprets laws and can declare them unconstitutional. 
 
 
 
• Legislative assembly
 
 
• Makes laws and procedures, and examines the administration and its resolutions. In a state with one house, it is known as the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
 
• In a state with two houses, the lower house is known as the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and the upper house is known as the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad). 
 
 
 
• Executive
 
 
• Implements the laws enacted by the legislature and enforces the will of the state. For example, the President enforces laws and has the power to veto legislation. 
 
 
• Separation of Powers in India: Executive, Legislature ...
 
• The separation of powers is the division of these functions among separate and independent bodies.
 
• The purpose of separation of powers is to limit the possibility of arbitrary excesses by the government

questions.question: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silicon**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silicon is the metalloid** among the given elements: 
 
• Silicon:
 
 
• **A metalloid is an element that has properties of both metals and nonmetals**.
 
 
 
• Silicon** has a metallic luster but is not a good conductor of electricity.**
 
• **Silicon is used to make alloys with iron and aluminum in the steel and automotive industries. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron:**

 
 
• It is a metal
 
• Symbol: Fe; Atomic number: 26.
 
• It is a strong, malleable, and ductile metal widely used in construction and manufacturing.
 
• It is essential for human health; a key component of haemoglobin in red blood cells.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen (O**)
 
 
• Symbol: O; Atomic number: 8.
 
• It is a colourless, odourless gas making up 21% of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It is Vital for respiration in living organisms; and supports combustion.
 
 
 
• **Sodium (Na)**
 
 
• Symbol: Na; Atomic number: 11.
 
• A soft, silvery metal that reacts vigorously with water.
 
• It is essential for nerve function and maintaining fluid balance

questions.question: Which country has the Republic feature of the Indian Constitution been borrowed from?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the French Constitution**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Republic feature of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the French Constitution:
 
 
• The ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity in the Indian Constitution's Preamble are from the French Constitution.
 
• These ideals emerged during the French Revolution.
 
• Democratic principles
 
• The Indian Constitution's emphasis on democratic principles, republicanism, and the sovereignty of the people can be traced back to the French Constitution. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution has also borrowed features from other countries, including:
 
• South African Constitution:
 
 
• The procedure for amending the Constitution and the election of members of Rajya Sabha 
 
 
 
• Japanese Constitution:
 
 
• The procedure established by law 
 
 
 
• Australian Constitution:
 
 
• The concurrent list, freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse, and joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament 
 
 
 
• Canadian Constitution:
 
 
• Federation with a strong center, vesting of residuary powers in the center, the appointment of state governors by the center, and advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court 
 
 
 
• Irish Constitution:
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy, nomination of members to Rajya Sabha, and the method of election of the president 
 
 
 
• Weimar Constitution of Germany:
 
 
• The suspension of fundamental rights during emergencies

questions.question:
Which of the following States has declared a social security scheme for registered newspaper hawkers in the State in 2021

considering the losses they faced during the pandemic and that they are a part of the unorganised sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of Odisha has announced a social security scheme specifically for registered newspaper hawkers in the state.
 
• This initiative was taken considering the financial losses that newspaper hawkers faced during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Newspaper hawkers are part of the unorganized sector, which often lacks the social security benefits available to organized workers.
 
• The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and security to newspaper hawkers to help them cope with their economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Social Security Schemes:**

 
 
• Social security schemes are government initiatives aimed at providing financial support and security to individuals, especially those in the unorganized sector.
 
• These schemes can include health insurance, pension plans, and financial aid during unemployment or economic hardships.
 
• Such initiatives are crucial for ensuring the well-being of workers who do not have access to formal employment benefits.
 
 
 
• **Unorganized Sector:**
 
 
• The unorganized sector refers to employment that is not regulated by the government and does not provide standard employment benefits like health insurance, retirement plans, or job security.
 
• Workers in this sector include daily wage laborers, agricultural workers, domestic workers, and small-scale vendors, among others.
 
• Due to the lack of formal employment benefits, workers in the unorganized sector are often vulnerable to economic instability.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Pandemic Impact:**
 
 
• The COVID-19 pandemic caused significant economic disruptions worldwide, affecting both organized and unorganized sectors.
 
• Many workers in the unorganized sector faced job losses, reduced income, and financial hardships due to lockdowns and restrictions.
 
• Governments around the world introduced various relief measures and social security schemes to support affected individuals and stabilize the economy.
 
 
 
• **Newspaper Hawkers:**
 
 
• Newspaper hawkers are individuals who distribute newspapers to households, offices, and other establishments.
 
• They play a vital role in ensuring the timely delivery of news and information to the public.
 
• Being part of the unorganized sector, newspaper hawkers often lack formal employment benefits and face economic challenges during crises like the pandemic.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main cause of land degradation in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deforestation due to mining**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The main cause of land degradation in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh is deforestation due to mining:
 
• Mining activities in these states have caused extensive damage to the land and environment.
 
• This is because mining involves deforestation, removal of topsoil, and excavation, which results in soil erosion, loss of fertility, and land degradation.
 
• Other factors
 
 
• Other factors that contribute to land degradation in these states include overgrazing, over-irrigation, and mineral processing.
 
 
 
• Sustainable practices
 
 
• To mitigate the negative impact of mining, sustainable mining practices, reforestation, and restoration of degraded lands are crucial.

questions.question: The Accelerated Female Literacy Programme was initiated in districts where the female literacy rate, based on the 2001 census, was ______:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**below 30%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Accelerated Female Literacy Programme was initiated in districts where the female literacy rate was **below 30%** based on the 2001 census.
 
• This initiative aimed to address the significant gender gap in literacy rates.
 
• The program focused on **empowering women through education**, which is crucial for social and economic development.
 
• It included various measures such as adult education centers, literacy campaigns, and skill development programs to improve female literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Female Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• The female literacy rate is the percentage of women who can read and write at a specified age, typically 15 years and older.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of gender equality and women’s empowerment.
 
• Higher literacy rates among women are associated with better health outcomes, lower fertility rates, and improved economic opportunities.
 
 
 
• **2001 Census:**
 
 
• The 2001 Census of India was the 14th census conducted in the country.
 
• It provided comprehensive data on various demographic parameters, including literacy rates, population distribution, and socio-economic indicators.
 
• The data from the census is used for planning and implementing various government policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Educational Initiatives for Women in India:**
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):** Launched in 2015, this campaign aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of girls.
 
• **Saakshar Bharat Mission:** Aimed at increasing adult literacy rates, particularly among women, by providing basic education and skill development.
 
• **National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level (NPEGEL):** Focuses on enhancing the education of girls in educationally backward blocks.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Female Education:**
 
 
• Educated women are more likely to participate in the workforce, contributing to economic growth.
 
• They are better equipped to make informed decisions about health, nutrition, and family planning.
 
• Female education contributes to overall social development and reduces gender disparities.

questions.question: As of 2021, which is the world's largest drainage basin with an area of about 70,00,000 km²?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Amazon Basin**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Amazon River Basin is the world's largest drainage basin, covering an area of about 7,000,000 square kilometers:
 
• The Amazon basin is located in the center and eastern parts of South America and includes parts of Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Suriname, French Guiana, and Venezuela.
 
• The Amazon basin is more than twice the size of the Congo River basin in Africa.
 
• It covers about 35.5% of the South American continent.
 
• The Amazon basin is home to the world's largest rainforest, which covers most of the basin and is also known as Amazonia.
 
• The Amazon rainforest is home to a huge variety of plant and animal species, including more than 40,000 plant species and 1,300 bird species.
 
• About one-fifth of all freshwater runoff on Earth passes through the Amazon basin. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Congo Basin: The world's second-largest river basin, located in west-central Africa: 
 
 
• It Covers over 1.3 million square miles (3.4 million square km) 
 
• It is the Home to the world's second-largest tropical rainforest, which is home to many endangered species, including gorillas, elephants, and chimpanzees 
 
• It Provides water for agriculture and energy generation 
 
• The Congo Basin is home to eight World Heritage Sites, including five that are in danger 
 
 
 
• Amur Basin:
 
 
• It Drains an area of about 716,200 square miles (1,855,000 square km) 
 
 
 
• Nile Basin:
 
 
• It Drains an area of about 1,293,000 square miles (3,349,000 square kilometers) 
 
• It Includes parts of Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Sudan, and Egypt 
 
• The longest river in the world, flowing through northeastern Africa and draining into the Mediterranean Sea

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is NOT of Aves?

options.text: They give birth to live young ones with some exceptions those lay eggs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They give birth to live young ones with some exceptions those lay eggs**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The characteristic that is not of Aves is giving birth to live young ones with some exceptions those lay eggs:
 
• Aves are oviparous, meaning they lay eggs, while mammals are viviparous, meaning they give birth to live young.
 
• The only mammals that lay eggs are the platypus and the echidnas. 
 
• Some other characteristics of Aves include:
 
 
• They are warm-blooded animals 
 
• They have a four-chambered heart 
 
• They have feathers covering their bodies 
 
• Their forelimbs are modified into wings 
 
• They breathe through lungs 
 
• They have no teeth 
 
• They have sharp eyesight 
 
• They have a modified beak made from their upper and lower jaws

questions.question: In which of the following states is the development of rail transport less, due to its geographical conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sikkim** has limited rail transport development due to its **challenging geographical conditions**, such as:

 
 
• **Mountainous terrain** and steep slopes.
 
• **Dense forests** and fragile ecosystems.
 
• Lack of large plains suitable for laying railway tracks.
 
 
 
• Sikkim is a small Himalayan state with mountainous terrain.
 
• This makes it difficult and expensive to construct and maintain railway tracks.
 
• The challenging topography limits the potential for rail transport development in the state.
 
• While Sikkim is working on developing its first railway line, the Sivok-Rangpo railway project, the state's geographical conditions pose significant challenges to rail transport development.

questions.question: Who among the following was a poet who won Nobel Prize for literature in 1913?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rabindranath Tagore__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913: 
 
• Tagore was a poet, writer, artist, and lyricist from Bengal.
 
• His work was rooted in both Indian and Western learning traditions.
 
• He wrote poetry, songs, stories, dramas, literary criticism, philosophy, and social issues. 
 
• Tagore won the Nobel Prize for his "profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse".
 
• The prize was awarded for his book of song offerings, Gitanjali. 
 
• Tagore was the first person from India and Asia to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
 
• He was also the first non-European to receive the award. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Aurobindo Ghose (Sri Aurobindo):
 
 
• Aurobindo Ghose, commonly known as Sri Aurobindo, was a prominent Indian philosopher, poet, and nationalist.
 
• He was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and later became a spiritual leader.
 
• Sri Aurobindo played an essential role in the early years of India's struggle for freedom from British rule and is known for his writings on spiritual evolution, the nature of the universe, and the role of human beings in achieving higher states of consciousness.
 
• His major works include The Life Divine and Savitri, an epic poem.
 
• Aurobindo also founded the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry, which became a center for spiritual learning.
 
 
 
• Rudyard Kipling:
 
 
• Rudyard Kipling was a British author and poet, best known for his works related to British India.
 
• He was born in 1865 and is famous for books like The Jungle Book, Kim, and poems such as If— and Gunga Din.
 
• Kipling's writings often dealt with themes of British imperialism, colonialism, and the relationship between the British and the Indian people.
 
• His work earned him the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1907.
 
 
 
• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay:
 
 
• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was a Bengali writer, poet, and journalist, known for his contributions to literature and his role in the Indian nationalist movement.
 
• He is best known for writing the national song Vande Mataram, which became a rallying cry for India's independence movement.
 
• His novel Anandamath (1882) is also notable for its portrayal of Bengali culture and history.

questions.question:
Which cell organelle is defined as the small round organelle that undergoes oxidation reaction to produce hydrogen

peroxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peroxisomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Peroxisomes - **

 
 
• Peroxisomes are small, membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes involved in various metabolic reactions, including the oxidation of fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• These organelles play a crucial role in detoxifying harmful substances and in lipid metabolism.
 
• They produce hydrogen peroxide as a byproduct of these reactions, which is then broken down by the enzyme catalase.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Centrosome

 
 
• Centrosome was discovered by T. Boberi in 1888.
 
• In almost all types of colonocytes except the nerve cell, a star-like structure is visible in the cytoplasm near the nucleus, which is called the centrosome.
 
• It helps in cell division,
 
• Forms cilia and flagellum and makes the tail of spermatozoa.
 
 

 
• **Vacuole**

 
 
• Vacuole__ is surrounded by the __tonoplast__, a type of cytoplasmic membrane that can stretch and fills itself with a solution known as cell sap
 
• Vacuoles are found mainly in plant cells and are filled with water, containing inorganic and organic molecules.
 
 

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• The nucleus is a pivotal organelle responsible to regulate almost all forms of cellular activities.
 
• Mostly, every type of cell that exists is categorized on the basis of the absence or presence of the nucleus within its cell (categorized either as a prokaryotic or eukaryotic cell.)

questions.question: The cause of a redox reaction is the:

options.text: transfer of electrons between two reactants
transfer of electrons between two products
transfer of neutrons between two reactants
exchange of halogens between two reactants

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transfer of electrons between two reactants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Redox Reactions

__
 
• Redox reactions are chemical reactions in which the oxidation states of atoms are changed.
 
• These reactions involve the transfer of electrons from one substance to another.
 
• One substance is oxidized (losing electrons) and another is reduced (gaining electrons).

Explanation:-__

 
• Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu

 
 
• Zn goes from 0 to +2 oxidation state (oxidation).
 
• Cu goes from +2 to 0 oxidation state (reduction).
 
• This is a redox reaction.
 
 
 
• 2KClO3 + I2 → 2KIO3 + Cl2
 
 
• Cl in KClO3 goes from +5 to 0 oxidation state (reduction).
 
• I in I2 goes from 0 to +5 oxidation state in KIO3 (oxidation).
 
• This is a redox reaction.
 
 
 
• H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl
 
 
• H goes from 0 to +1 oxidation state (oxidation).
 
• Cl goes from 0 to -1 oxidation state (reduction).
 
• This is a redox reaction.

questions.question: ‘Sangken’ is a festival celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh by people of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddhism**

 
 
• Gautama Buddha, variously termed Sakyamuni or Tathagata, is considered as the founder of Buddhism.
 
• He was born as Siddhartha to Suddhodhana, the ruler of the Sakyan republic, and his wife Maya, on Vaisakha Purnima in the Lumbini gardens near Kapilavasthu (in Nepal) in the 6th century BC.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jainism**

 
 
• Jainism is one of the world’s oldest living religions.
 
• Jainism grounds itself in 24 Tirthankaras.
 
• A ‘Tirthankara’, is the one who revealed religious truth at different times.
 
• The first Tirthankara was Rishabhadev.
 
• The last and 24th tirthankara of the Jainas was Mahaveer Swami or Vardhamana Mahavira.
 
• Jainism gained prominence under the aegis of Mahavira, during the sixth century BC.
 
• He was a kshatriya prince of the Lichchhavis, a group that was part of the Vajji sangha.
 
• At the age of thirty, he left home and went to live in a forest.
 
• For twelve years he led a hard and lonely life, at the end of which he attained enlightenment.
 
• The followers of Mahavira were known as Jainas.
 
• The teachings of Mahavira and his followers were transmitted orally for several centuries.
 
• 
 
They were written down in the form in which they are presently available at a place called Valabhi, in Gujarat, about 1500 years ago.

questions.question: What is the aim of the PM Ujjwala 2.0 Yojna launched in August 2021?

options.text: Free LPG connections for commercial use
20 million LPG connections will be provided to the beneficiaries
10 million LPG connections will be provided to the beneficiaries
Free gas stove for BPL Households

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 million LPG connections will be provided to the beneficiaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched Ujjwala 2.0 (Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana - PMUY) by handing over LPG connections, at Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh__ on 10th August 2021.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Ujjwala 1.0 was launched in 2016 and the target was set to provide LPG connections to five crore women members of BPL households.
 
• Subsequently, the scheme was expanded in April 2018 to include women beneficiaries from seven more categories: SC/ST, PMAY, AAY, Most backward classes, tea garden, forest dwellers, Islands.
 
• In the Union budget for FY 21-22, provision for an additional one crore LPG connection under the PMUY scheme was announced.
 
• These one crore additional PMUY connections (under Ujjwala 2.0) aim to provide deposit-free LPG connections to those low-income families who could not be covered under the earlier phase of PMUY.
 
• Along with a deposit free LPG connection, Ujjwala 2.0 will provide the first refill and hotplate free of cost to the beneficiaries. Also, the enrollment procedure will require minimal paperwork.

questions.question: If assets of a bank are greater than liabilities, it will be recorded as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**net worth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Net worth is a financial metric that represents the overall value of an individual, company, or entity.
 
• It's calculated by subtracting total liabilities from total assets.
 
• A positive net worth indicates financial health, while a negative one signifies debt exceeding assets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assets: **

 
 
• These are items of value owned by an individual or entity, such as real estate, vehicles, investments, bank accounts, and personal belongings.
 
 
 
• **Liabilities: **
 
 
• These are financial obligations or debts, including mortgages, loans, credit card debt, and other outstanding payments.

questions.question: Which of the following departments of Delhi Sultanate was reorganized by Balban?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Diwan-i-Arz__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Balban **created the department of **Diwan-i-Arz** in Delhi Sultanate.
 
• **Diwan-i-Arz**
 
 
• Diwan-i-Arz was essentially the Department of Military managed by Ariz-i-Mamalik. 
 
• He was accountable for the regulation and preservation of the royal army.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administration under the Sultanate:**

 
 
• It was also influenced by the Iranian system of administration.
 
• The situation in India and Indian traditions was kept in mind during these systems.
 
• **Organs of the Government:**
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Wizarat:**
 
 
• Department of revenue and finance headed by the Wazir.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Arz:**
 
 
• Department of Military headed by Ariz-i-Mamalik.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i- Insha:**
 
 
• Department of royal correspondence headed by Dabir-i-lnsha.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Risalat:**
 
 
• Department of religious affairs headed by the chief Qazi.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-bandagan:**
 
 
• **​**Diwan-i-bandagan (department of slaves) and Diwan-i-Khairat (charity department) was created by Firuz Shah Tughluq. 
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-mustakharaj:**
 
 
• Diwan-i-mustakharaj (to realise arrears) was created by Alauddin Khiiji. 
 
 
 
• **Diwan- i-kohi:**
 
 
• Diwan- i-kohi (department of agriculture) was created by Muhammad bin Tughluq.
